For Level 1 shore-zone mapping, unsupervised classification of the temporal and composite indices achieved overall mapping accuracies of 56–73% for the Upper Shore Zone across three study areas. For Level 2 shoreline-type mapping, Random Forest classification of high-resolution satellite imagery, including WorldView and GeoEye imagery, achieved overall accuracies of 81–85% across the four study areas. These results demonstrate the potential of the composite shore-zone proxy to integrate complementary SAR and optical information for consistent characterization of Arctic shore zones, while the subsequent shoreline-type classification provides additional geomorphological detail. Together, the hierarchical products provide spatially explicit shoreline information that can support the identification and prioritization of shoreline areas for oil-spill response planning and resource allocation.

title: Unraveling Spatial Associations of Surface Subsidence in Typical Oil Production Areas of Songyuan City by Integrating Time-Series InSAR and Deep Learning
summary: Oilfield subsidence threatens infrastructure and sustainable development. Although facility detection, factor-association analysis, and deformation forecasting have each advanced considerably, their systematic integration remains insufficiently explored for oilfields in agricultural plains, where C-band SAR decorrelation over cropland and wetland yields sparse and uneven deformation observations. This constraint complicates facility extraction, quantitative analysis of associations among interacting factors, and robust temporal prediction. To address these challenges, this study develops and applies an integrated modular workflow for the monitoring, analysis and prediction of surface subsidence in a typical oil production area of Songyuan City, China. We first used PS-InSAR for high-precision deformation monitoring and validated the results with leveling survey data. Subsequently, the YOLOv12 model was utilized for automated oil well identification, and the Geodetector model was applied to quantify the spatial associations between subsidence and the examined natural and anthropogenic factors. Finally, a hybrid LSTM–Transformer model was developed for time-series prediction and applied to forecast deformation through November 2025, twelve months beyond the final SAR acquisition. Results indicate significant spatial differentiation in deformation, with a maximum subsidence rate of −26.0 mm/y. Analysis identifies oil well density and surface elevation as the leading spatial factors among those examined, and the buffer zone analysis indicates a distance-related association of approximately 700 m between oil wells and subsidence rates. The hybrid model demonstrated superior overall accuracy compared to standalone LSTM and Transformer models. The findings provide concrete scientific support for risk mitigation in oil cities.

title: Optical Multispectral Indices Versus Microwave-Based Soil Water Index for Surface Soil Moisture Assessment: A Linear Mixed-Effects Analysis of Pixel-Level Heterogeneity over a Tuscan Agricultural Landscape
summary: Soil moisture (SM) assessment underpins applications ranging from climatological studies to land management and emergency response. Microwave techniques already support operational SM products, but at a spatial resolution limited to 1 km. Optical multispectral indices have been proposed as a complementary source of information at finer resolutions (10–100 m), yet vegetation heterogeneity has generally been handled by masking or stratifying the land cover rather than by modeling its effect. Here, we compare three indices (the Normalized Difference Infrared Index, NDII; the Normalized Multi-band Drought Index, NMDI; and the Visible and Shortwave Infrared Drought Index, VSDI) over a heterogeneous agricultural area near Grosseto, Tuscany, using 31 Landsat-8 OLI images acquired over four summers. Evaluated against the Copernicus Soil Water Index (SWI), VSDI performed best both when averaged over the test area and when analyzed at the pixel level (1 km) and was therefore selected for further analysis. A linear mixed-effects model with pixel-dependent intercepts resolves a within-pixel VSDI–SWI repeated measures correlation of 0.714, against 0.411 for the pooled regression. Allowing the slope to vary as well shows that vegetation density governs both the baseline level of VSDI and its sensitivity to soil moisture, with the within-pixel correlation falling from 0.84 on bare soil to 0.30 under a dense canopy.

title: A Transformer Network for Settlement Generalization Integrating Raster Maps and Remote Sensing Images
summary: To address the challenges of reliance on manual expertise and insufficient automation and intelligence in settlement generalization during scale transformation, this paper proposes a multi-scale settlement generalization model (DSG-Trans) based on the fusion of dual-source data: raster maps and remote sensing images. Leveraging the cartographic correspondence between remote sensing image resolution and map scale, this model integrates source-scale maps with specific low-resolution remote sensing imagery to automatically generate target-scale raster maps that adhere to cartographic specifications. The model employs a bidirectional cross-attention mechanism and a Transformer architecture to facilitate the semantic integration of dual-source data, while a progressive upsampling strategy is utilized to reconstruct spatial details. Additionally, a composite loss function incorporating four constraints is designed to enhance the quality of settlement generalization. Experiments were conducted in New York City, USA, using a multi-source dataset constructed from 3D-GloBFP building footprint data and multi-source remote sensing imagery, focusing on two scale transformation scenarios: 1:5000 to 1:10,000 and 1:5000 to 1:25,000. The results indicate that the proposed method effectively learns and simulates expert generalization knowledge, significantly improving the automation level and scale adaptability of map generalization while preserving geometric morphology and spatial distribution patterns.

title: 3DMAUNet: A 3D Memory-Augmented Deep Unfolding Network with Dynamic Momentum Updating for Snapshot Compressive Spectral Imaging
summary: Coded aperture snapshot spectral compressive imaging (CASSI) enables the recovery of hyperspectral images (HSIs) from a single two-dimensional compressive measurement, serving as a core paradigm in modern computational imaging. However, HSI reconstruction from under-sampled measurements is a severely ill-posed inverse problem. Existing deep unfolding methods typically treat each iterative stage independently and model spatial–spectral features in a decoupled manner, which neglects intrinsic spatial–spectral coupling and lacks persistent cross-stage information propagation. To tackle these issues, we propose a deep dynamic 3D memory-augmented unfolding network (3DMAUNet) for HSI reconstruction. Based on the momentum-accelerated generalized alternating projection framework, 3DMAUNet retains the strict mathematical interpretability of iterative optimization while integrating data-driven learnable components. Specifically, we design two key modules: (1) a 3D memory-augmented learning module equipped with a persistent memory bank, which explicitly encodes cross-layer spatial–spectral correlations to enable efficient inter-stage information transfer and long-range dependency modeling; and (2) a learnable dynamic fast momentum updating module, which fuses cross-stage spatial–spectral attention features to estimate task-adaptive momentum coefficients, accelerating convergence and enhancing the robustness of feature updating. Comprehensive experiments on synthetic and real-world HSI datasets demonstrate that 3DMAUNet outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both quantitative and qualitative reconstruction performance.

title: High-resolution Antarctic sea surface temperatures from Landsat enabled by cloud-native processing and novel seal-tag validation
summary: Ocean heat transport drives approximately half of Antarctic ice mass loss, yet in situ ocean observations near glacier ice fronts remain exceedingly scarce given the challenges of data collection in this remote environment. Remotely sensed sea surface temperatures (SST) offer a powerful alternative, but no reliable product resolves the fine spatial resolution needed to observe partially ice-covered coastal Antarctic seas. Here, we develop and validate an efficient, open-source, cloud-native single-channel SST algorithm for Landsat 8, designed for Antarctic conditions and transferable to previous Landsat sensors carrying a thermal infrared band. Cross-calibration with MODIS SSTs yields a root mean square error of 0.26 ∘ C. For comparison, we apply the existing Landsat Surface Temperature algorithm to the same scenes with an assumed ocean emissivity, since that product is not generated south of 60 ∘ S. This approach yields an RMSE ∼ 30% larger than our algorithm, consistent with the reduced accuracy expected for land-heritage algorithms over water. Independent validation using 6 Argo-float-derived and 81 seal-tag-derived measurements shows strong agreement, with an RMSE of 0.22 ∘ C for SST retrievals spanning from −1.9 to 1.0 ∘ C. Given the dearth of Argo observations, we find that seal-borne sensors represent an untapped resource for validating high-resolution polar SST, with no degradation in quality even with larger location uncertainties. Using this product, we present the first SST retrieval of a sub-kilometer Antarctic meltwater plume. This new Antarctic SST product provides a high-resolution thermal record extending back to 2013, opening new opportunities to study polar ice-ocean interactions.

title: Effectiveness of multi-source merged soil moisture products using different triple collocation methods: A comprehensive assessment incorporating spatial similarity evaluation framework
summary: Evaluation of soil moisture products and data merging efforts have commonly focused on their performance in representing temporal dynamics, while overlooking the capacity of the products to capture spatial patterns. In this study, a spatial evaluation framework based on the Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) was for the first time introduced to assess the behavior of soil moisture products. Meanwhile, a modified temporal-spatial triple collocation (TC) merging method that accounts for local spatial errors (referred to as TC_2D_local) was proposed for merging multi-source soil moisture. Three widely used soil moisture products, i.e. Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP), Advanced SCATterometer (ASCAT), and ERA5-Land, as well as their merged products based on three TC approaches, including the traditional TC (TC_temporal), a global two-dimensional TC (TC_2D), and the new TC_2D_local, were evaluated and compared from both temporal and spatial perspectives, using conventional metrics (R, RMSE, Bias, ubRMSE), together with SSIM and its component indices, i.e. Similarity in Mean (SIM), Similarity in Variance (SIV) and Similarity in Pattern (SIP). Soil moisture from International Soil Moisture Network (ISMN), agricultural stations and China Meteorological Administration Land Data Assimilation System (CLDAS) were used for validation. The results revealed the distinct behavior of the three parent products in capturing temporal dynamics and spatial patterns of soil moisture over China. SMAP achieved the lowest RMSE and highest SSIM in western China, while ERA5-Land was superior in southeastern China in both temporal and spatial evaluation, with larger values of R and SSIM. Although ASCAT exhibited a less satisfactory temporal performance with lower R and higher RMSE, it better characterized the spatial variability of soil moisture with higher SIV across China. All of the TC merged products demonstrated improvements with a reduced RMSE and Bias, while the two 2D TC approaches that incorporated spatial error information outperformed TC_temporal. However, TC_2D performed better in the eastern part of China, featured by relatively uniform underlying conditions, whereas TC_2D_local yielded lower RMSE and Bias in western China, which has more sophisticated environmental conditions. SSIM-based spatial evaluation further revealed a consistent superiority of TC_2D_local over TC_temporal and TC_2D, achieving SIM > 0.95, SIV > 0.9, SIP >0.95 and SSIM >0.8 across most of the study area, with the most pronounced improvements in western China. This study demonstrated the effectiveness of two-dimensional TC for merging multi-source soil moisture products, particularly the TC_2D_local for environmentally heterogeneous regions. It was highlighted that the spatial similarity evaluation framework could provide a new perspective and additional insights into the performance of soil moisture products, potentially benefiting their applications such as hydrological modelling and agricultural drought monitoring, which requires accurate representation of spatial soil moisture patterns.

title: Integrated retrieval of ocean surface wind and current fields from single-geometry SAR observations through a physically constrained Bayesian framework
summary: Ocean surface winds and currents are coupled through air–sea interaction but are commonly retrieved independently from spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR). For operational single-geometry SAR, simultaneous wind–current retrieval is underdetermined and remains reliant on background information. We propose a physically constrained Bayesian framework that combines radar backscatter and Doppler centroid anomaly measurements to retrieve 10-m wind and radial surface current. An empirical wind-drift relation softly constrains the radial-current increment relative to a product-derived background current, and the solution is obtained by weighted maximum a posteriori estimation. The framework is evaluated using multi-year Sentinel-1 observations collocated with scatterometer, buoy, and high-frequency radar measurements across different sea states. Parameters calibrated in a Gulf Stream-influenced U.S. East Coast region are fixed for temporally held-out events and an independent Southern California test. Across the East Coast data, wind-speed root-mean-square difference (RMSD) decreases by 0.59 − 0.77 m s − 1 relative to ERA5 atmospheric reanalysis. Against high-frequency radar, radial-current RMSD is 0.21 m s − 1 , compared with 0.59 m s − 1 for the operational Sentinel-1 radial-velocity product, 0.48 m s − 1 after a conventional wind-wave Doppler correction, and 0.38 m s − 1 for an ocean-model projection. Event-level ablations show that the physical constraint provides further RMSD reductions of 0.171 m s − 1 and 0.324 m s − 1 in the two independent tests. These results isolate radial-current skill attributable to the physical term beyond joint data fusion alone and demonstrate the value of jointly exploiting complementary SAR observables. The framework provides a practical pathway toward joint kilometer-scale mapping of coastal winds and radial currents from routine single-geometry acquisitions.

title: Mapping subsurface combustion cavities in underground coal fires using nonlocal DS-InSAR and physics-based inversion
summary: Underground coal fires threaten environmental sustainability, resource conservation, and infrastructure safety, yet their concealed nature makes subsurface combustion processes difficult to characterize using a single observation technique. In this paper, we present an integrated remote sensing framework combining deformation and thermal observations with physics-based inversion to investigate underground coal-fire dynamics in the Shuixigou coalfield, Xinjiang, China. First, a nonlocal distributed scatterer InSAR approach was applied to 32 Sentinel-1A images spanning January 2018 to December 2019, yielding high-density time-series line-of-sight deformation. Meanwhile, Landsat-8 thermal infrared imagery was processed using a generalized single-channel algorithm to derive time-series land surface temperature. Moreover, we characterized the spatiotemporal evolution of coal-fire activity through a joint analysis of the deformation and thermal time series. Furthermore, the cumulative deformation field was then incorporated into an Okada rectangular dislocation model with a smooth regularization constraint, yielding the geometry of equivalent combustion cavities. In our experimental coal-mining area, two major subsidence basins were identified, with maximum cumulative line-of-sight displacements of approximately −160 mm and −120 mm. Besides, the inferred combustion sources were located at depths of 53.11 m and 80.65 m, consistent with independent geophysical survey estimates of 56.0 m and 85.5 m. Combined analysis further reveals that long-term combustion zones are associated with concentrated subsidence, while thermal anomalies preferentially occur along fracture systems surrounding subsidence centers, indicating distinct thermal and mechanical responses.

title: The conditional nature of error estimates in multi-source satellite SIF cross-evaluation: How product combinations, statistical models, spatial scales, and temporal treatments shape the conclusions
summary: Cross-evaluation results of multi-source satellite solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF) products depend critically on the analytical choices made during evaluation, including product combinations, statistical models, and spatiotemporal preprocessing. This study constructs a diagnostic framework to systematically assess the methodological sensitivity of cross-evaluation. Using four representative SIF products from 2018 to 2021, we isolated the independent effects of product combination, error model (Three-Cornered Hat, TCH, vs. Quadruple Collocation Analysis, QCA), spatial aggregation scale, and seasonal-cycle treatment through controlled experiments. Direct comparison showed the closest agreement between the two TROPOMI products, whereas GOME-2 SIF showed the largest discrepancies. A key finding is that when a product combination includes two products that share observations from the same sensor, TCH produces a structural bias due to violation of the error-independence assumption: it systematically underestimates the errors of the shared-source products while overestimating the errors of the independent product. Allowing a prescribed non-zero error covariance between the shared-source pair, QCA mitigated this bias. Under QCA, more than 97% of valid vegetated grid cells for OCO-2 SIF, TROPOSIF Caltech , and TROPOSIF ESA had RMSE below 0.2 mW·m −2 ·sr −1 ·nm −1 , whereas more than 77% of GOME-2 grid cells fell within 0.2–0.4 mW·m −2 ·sr −1 ·nm −1 . Coarser-resolution products were more sensitive to spatial aggregation, while seasonal-cycle removal reduced error estimates for all products, with the largest reduction (~52%) for OCO-2 SIF. These results show that cross-evaluation error estimates reflect both product-specific error characteristics and the analytical framework under which they are derived. The framework is transferable to uncertainty analyses of other satellite-retrieved geophysical variables.

title: An optimized methane retrieval approach based on morphological fusion for mapping methane point emissions from spaceborne imaging spectrometry
summary: Methane (CH 4 ) emissions from point sources in the energy sector play a crucial role in the global CH 4 budget. Spaceborne imaging spectrometry has demonstrated superior capability for monitoring such events over large areas and extended periods. At present, the data-driven Matched Filter (MF) technique has been widely employed for satellite-based retrieval of CH 4 emission rates. However, the traditional single-channel MF approach often omits small plumes and underestimates fluxes, introducing significant uncertainties in the CH 4 inventories for the energy industry at the global scale. Here, we propose a morphological fusion matched-filter algorithm (Fused-MF) that spatially decouples plume detection from concentration quantification. A full-shortwave infrared MF (SWMF) is first used to produce a low-noise map of the column-averaged dry-air mole fraction of CH 4 (XCH 4 ) enhancement relative to the background (ΔXCH 4 ) to delineate the plume through morphological segmentation. Within the resulting mask, ΔXCH 4 values are then retrieved by a lognormal MF (LMF) corrected with a sensor-specific effective factor ( k SRF ), whereas SWMF result is retained outside the mask. This design preserves the operational efficiency of scene-wide MF screening while reducing the systematic underestimation of large ΔXCH 4 values. The proposed algorithm is validated via two-stage assessments. First, retrieval accuracy for ΔXCH 4 is assessed using end-to-end simulation. Second, hyperspectral observations from Chinese Gaofen 5B, Ziyuan 1F, Italian PRISMA, and German EnMAP are used to retrieve CH 4 emissions from a ground-based controlled-release experiment using our proposed Fused-MF and traditional MF algorithms. We then compare the retrieval results with ground-based measurements to evaluate our method's performance in estimating the CH 4 emission rate. The results from end-to-end simulations show that the Fused-MF method achieves the most accurate ΔXCH 4 quantification among the four methods evaluated, yielding a near-unity regression slope of 0.98, a BIAS of −8.48 ppb, an root-mean-square-error (RMSE) of 43.17 ppb, and a mean absolute error (MAE) of 34.02 ppb. Scenario-level statistics across 36 simulations confirm that its reduction in retrieval error is significant relative to all three single-channel methods. Further analysis using the field controlled-release experiment data reveals the capability of the Fused-MF method to detect minor CH 4 emissions that traditional MF methods fail to identify. Meanwhile, the Fused-MF-based emission rate quantifications show an R 2 of 0.99 and an RMSE of 0.19 t(CH 4 )/h, representing reductions of approximately 36.7% in RMSE, 56.0% in MAE, and 33.3% in standard deviation (STD) compared with the mostly used MF method applying spectral channel with strong CH 4 absorption signal (SAMF). We further apply the Fused-MF algorithm to Gaofen 5/5A/5B imagery acquired between 2019 and 2023 over the Delaware Basin (United States), Libya, Algeria, Oman, and Shanxi (China). Sixteen plumes are identified through case studies, confirming the Fused-MF algorithm's robust capability to detect and quantify CH 4 point-source emissions from the energy sector.

title: Comparison of NASA Harmonized Landsat and Sentinel-2 (HLS) surface reflectance products with MODIS NBAR
summary: Frequent surface reflectance measurements at fine spatial resolutions are crucial for land surface monitoring. The NASA Harmonized Landsat and Sentinel-2 (HLS) project addresses this need by combining data from Landsat and Sentinel-2 missions to provide 30-m surface reflectance products with a global average revisit frequency of 2-3 days. This study evaluates the consistency of the HLS Version 2 (V2.0) product against the established Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) Nadir Bidirectional Reflectance Distribution Function-Adjusted Reflectance (NBAR) dataset. We found a high degree of consistency between HLS and MODIS NBAR, with strong positive correlations across all six common spectral bands (R 2 values: 0.939–0.986). Globally, mean absolute differences (MADs) were generally low, typically under 0.03 for visible bands and below 0.05 for NIR and SWIR bands. However, we observed band-dependent discrepancies, with higher discrepancies in the blue and SWIR1 bands. Spatially, substantial differences were found in polar regions, largely due to isolated snow, ice, and water which are fractional and hard to detect within the coarser MODIS pixels but are filtered out in the HLS data. This finding suggests a potential explanation for past disagreements in vegetation trend analyses involving the use of satellite data of different spatial resolutions, as coarser-resolution datasets may mischaracterize greening trends in areas with partial snow and ice cover. These insights are vital for helping users interpret HLS data more effectively and for refining multi-sensor data fusion methods. Our research also provides a valuable baseline for ongoing quality assessment of the HLS product for applications such as vegetation monitoring, land management, and disaster response.

title: Methodology for assessing the accuracy of long-term, annual land cover monitoring at national scale: Experiences from the Land Change Monitoring, Assessment, and Projection (LCMAP) initiative
summary: Annual land cover monitoring using medium-resolution satellite imagery represents a transition from periodic mapping campaigns to continuous observation systems. This transition introduces accuracy assessment challenges not encountered in one-time mapping efforts, particularly when the initial monitoring period is extended forward in time. These challenges are not addressed in existing guidance, which remains largely framed around the evaluation of maps of a single date or maps showing changes between two dates. We present a set of methodological adaptations to adjust to this evolving paradigm, using as a case study the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) Land Change Monitoring, Assessment, and Projection (LCMAP) initiative, which generated annual land cover and land cover change products across the historical Landsat archive. Assessing the accuracy of these products was an essential component of LCMAP and resulted in an extensive reference sample dataset that may be used for accuracy estimation, area estimation, or support in the development of new algorithms or models. We review the LCMAP methodology and highlight challenges encountered and lessons learned that are transferable to other long-term, temporally dense monitoring programs. This framework demonstrates that statistically rigorous assessment can scale to operational annual land cover production, while the experiences of the project clarify where existing good practice guidance should be extended to support the needs of ongoing, continuous land cover monitoring.

title: Underwater topographic mapping using a fusion of Airborne LiDAR bathymetry and multibeam Echo sounding
summary: Accurate measurement of underwater topography is of significant importance for maritime affairs, marine resource development, and environmental protection. Airborne LiDAR Bathymetry (ALB) can efficiently acquire integrated above-water and underwater data in shallow water areas, while the Multibeam Echo-sounding System (MBES) can precisely measure underwater topography in deep water areas and some shallow water regions. By integrating underwater acoustic and optical data, an integrated above-water and underwater topographic representation can be achieved. However, due to differences in measurement ranges, point cloud accuracy, and density, existing fusion algorithms perform poorly in combining ALB and MBES point clouds. This paper proposes a point cloud fusion method suitable for ALB and MBES data. The proposed method first uses a virtual grid combined with the alpha shape algorithm to quickly determine the overlapping area and removes edge triangles using boundary points, reducing the influence of edge triangles. Then, to minimize the impact of topographic differences on coarse point cloud registration, a point-to-plane ICP (Iterative Closest Point) algorithm based on TIN (Triangulated Irregular Network) grid vertex cutting planes is applied, with weighting assigned to the points corresponding to the matching cutting plane’s grid vertices. To mitigate the impact of point cloud density, the distance loss term in the Non-Rigid ICP cost function is changed from a point-to-point distance loss term to a point-to-plane distance loss term. The root mean square error (RMSE) in three experimental regions decreased from 0.149 m, 0.185 m, and 0.217 m to 0.038 m, 0.035 m, and 0.078 m. For comparative analysis, classical Non-Rigid ICP and TrICP (Trimmed Iterative Closest Point) algorithms are implemented using the same preprocessing procedures. The results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves better performance than both the Non-Rigid ICP and TrICP approaches in terms of geometric consistency. These results demonstrate the advantages of the proposed method in terms of both accuracy and robustness when applied to complex scenarios.

title: VLM-Mapper: Multimodal vision-language models for prior guided lane-level HD map construction
summary: The automated construction of High-Definition (HD) maps from remote sensing data is essential for modern intelligent transportation systems and spatial data infrastructure. While imagery provides a scalable solution for lane-level HD map construction, traditional discriminative models often struggle in complex scenarios because of their reliance on local visual features and limited use of external geographic context. To address these limitations, this paper introduces VLM-Mapper, a framework that reframes lane-level HD map construction as a multimodal sequence-generation task based on visual–language alignment and prior-conditioned token generation. VLM-Mapper systematically integrates high-resolution aerial imagery with tokenized geographic prior prompts, including standard map metadata and boundary entry points, to guide HD map construction. Furthermore, to mitigate the spatial inconsistencies and count errors of autoregressive decoding, we implement a two-stage post-training pipeline. This strategy establishes spatial alignment via Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT), followed by a Reinforcement Learning (RL) phase using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with a custom geometry-aware and numerical reward function. Experimental results on the large-scale OpenSatMap dataset show that VLM-Mapper achieves state-of-the-art performance and improves the robustness and topological consistency of HD map construction across large-scale aerial imagery.

title: GGFA-SwinIR: A gradient-guided and frequency-aware joint multi-scale framework for bathymetric DEM super-resolution
summary: High-resolution bathymetric digital elevation models (DEMs) support marine geoscience, but global grids can smooth fine-scale terrain where observations are sparse. We present GGFA-SwinIR (Gradient-Guided Frequency-Aware SwinIR), a shared-backbone discrete multi-scale framework for × 2 , × 4 , and × 8 reference-grid reconstruction. The framework integrates gradient-magnitude guidance, bicubic-base residual prediction, and pixel, gradient, and complex-spectrum supervision. Under bicubic degradation of GEBCO_2025, GGFA-SwinIR achieved H-RMSE values of 5.13, 9.82, and 18.90 m and PSNR values of 70.28, 65.48, and 59.84 dB at × 2 , × 4 , and × 8 , respectively. In a four-severity low-pass diagnostic, GGFA-SwinIR achieved the lowest H-RMSE and highest PSNR among six methods in all 12 severity-scale conditions and the lowest slope-angle RMSE in 11. Cross-product transfer comparisons with GMRT v4.3 showed the lowest H-RMSE across two evaluation regions and three scales. These results demonstrate the value of jointly modelling terrain gradients and spectral structure for multi-scale bathymetric reference-grid reconstruction and provide an empirically validated basis for exploratory grid enhancement.

title: WMoE-Net: wavelet-directed cross-attention alignment with mixture-of-experts network for multimodal SAR-optical ship detection
summary: Multisource remote-sensing fusion benefits port and near-shore ship surveillance: optical images provide rich textures in daylight, while SAR remains informative in day-and-night and all-weather conditions. Yet high-resolution SAR–optical ship detection is challenged by scarce near-simultaneous acquisitions, residual misalignment after co-registration, and condition-dependent modality degradation. We curate MSOSD-1.0, a high-resolution paired SAR–optical dataset for port/near-shore ship detection, containing 1,715 co-registered patch pairs with 17,915 oriented ship instances and diverse conditions (low illumination, clouds/fog, cluttered backgrounds). On this basis, we propose WMoE-Net, a correspondence-constrained and reliability-aware alignment–gating–fusion framework. A wavelet-directed cross-attention module (WCAM) enhances local correspondence under residual mismatch. A condition-informed quality gating network (CIQGN) performs sparse expert routing among optical-preferred, SAR-preferred, and collaborative-fusion branches, while a mutually-guided consistency-aware fusion expert (MCFM) refines the collaborative branch to enhance fusion quality. Experiments on MSOSD-1.0 and QXS-SAROPT-SHIP show consistent gains over strong single-modal and multimodal baselines, especially under low illumination and clouds/fog.

title: Quantile-based homogeneity selection and similarity-weighted robust coherence matrix for distributed scatterer interferometry in mining deformation monitoring
summary: Coal mining can lead to a series of geological issues, making it crucial to monitor surface deformation for early hazard warning in mining areas. Distributed Scatterer Interferometry (DSI) enables the monitoring of deformation in overlying strata above mining working faces. However, the accuracy of this technology is often affected by spatiotemporal decorrelation, necessitating phase recovery processing. The Phase Linking (PL) algorithm can effectively recover the interferometric phase, but it is limited by the correctness of statistical homogeneous pixel selection (SHPs) and the utilization of spatial dimensional information, making it difficult to obtain a sample complex coherence matrix (SCCM) that closely resembles the true situation. This severely impacts the accuracy of the PL estimation results. To address this, this paper proposes two solutions: (1) For SHPs, the medcouple (MC) method is used as a robust measure of skewed distributions, adjusting the boxplot to optimize homogeneous samples in the intensity map, removing outliers and enhancing sample robustness; (2) For SCCM construction, a similarity measure between reference pixels and homogeneous pixels is used as a weight, and a weighted sum with constraint processing is applied to obtain a robust coherence matrix. Simulation and real-world results show that the proposed method can recover phase information severely affected by noise, maintain phase stability, and significantly increase the monitoring point density; its high reliability has been validated through leveling data verification.

title: Tracking vegetation disturbance, recovery, and sustainability in open-pit mining areas of Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei Region from 2000 to 2024
summary: Evaluating the overarching efficacy of mine greening initiatives and supporting land resource management within open-pit mining areas requires accurate long-term monitoring of both vegetative degradation and its subsequent regenerative phases. Overcoming the bottlenecks of conventional methods in decoupling vegetation abrupt disturbances from gradual recovery processes, this research utilizes the Google Earth Engine (GEE) and Landsat data spanning from 2000 to 2024. The investigation explicitly targets open-pit mining areas across the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei region. Through the synergistic integration of the Continuous Change Detection and Classification (CCDC) and an adaptively refined NDVImed,t segmentation baseline, we extracted the spatiotemporal dynamics of abrupt vegetation disturbance and gradual recovery events. Furthermore, to rigorously quantify the enduring stability and long-term persistence of these vegetation dynamic trajectories, the study coupled the non-parametric Sen–MK trend estimator with calculations of the Hurst exponent. The results demonstrate that the F1 score for detecting disturbance and recovery events over the past 25 years stably exceeded 0.8, exhibiting excellent temporal robustness. The derived chronological trajectories pinpoint 2013 as a significant turning point for vegetation dynamics. Before this critical juncture, the landscape suffered from intense degradation, marked by an average annual vegetative deficit of 962.19 ha. In the post-2013 era, a recovery-dominated paradigm emerged, characterized by an average yearly restoration of 831.37 ha. Crucially, the aggregate intensity of this vegetation greenness reached 1.64, substantially overshadowing the historical extraction-induced disturbance magnitude of 1.23. Concurrently, evaluations of trajectory persistence reveal that while a substantial 36.56% of the monitored landscape is undergoing sustained ecological enhancement, whereas 22.46% was characterized by persistent deterioration. Precipitation and temperature showed a limited influence on vegetation dynamics (R2 = 0.0796, p = 0.402), while enterprise consolidation and reclamation policies were the main drivers for post-2013 recovery. The acquired quantitative remote sensing evidence not only reveals the core role of macro-policy regulation in driving the reshaping of surface landscapes in mining areas but also provides solid scientific support for the future refined ecological governance of regional territorial space.

title: How does hillside urban expansion affect the surface urban heat island effect? empirical evidence from China
summary: Global urbanization has driven the expansion of urban construction land into high-altitude areas. This hillside urban expansion (HUE) reshapes the underlying surface pattern and profoundly affects the formation and evolution of the surface urban heat island (SUHI) effect. However, the underlying mechanism by which HUE affects the SUHI effect has not been systematically elucidated. Based on multi-source remote sensing data from 2001 to 2023, this study constructed an urban climbing intensity comprehensive index (CICI) and an SUHI intensity index, and analyzed the spatio-temporal differentiation characteristics of HUE and the SUHI effect at the provincial, municipal, and county scales in China. A structural equation model, an interpretable random forest model, the optimal parameter geographical detector, and the geographical pattern causality model were then applied to reveal the mechanisms by which HUE affects the SUHI effect across the four quadrants demarcated by the Heihe–Tengchong Line and the Bole–Taipei Line (clockwise from Northeast China). The main findings are as follows: (1) The dynamic process of HUE at different scales was dominated by low-intensity expansion; the center of gravity of the static slope ratio was consistently located in the second quadrant (South and Southwest China), with its overall movement trajectory perpendicular to the Heihe–Tengchong Line during the study period. The proportion of medium- and high-intensity slope-climbing cities increased slowly, and high-intensity slope-climbing cities were mostly distributed in the second quadrant. (2) The distribution of SUHI intensity showed scale similarity and regional heterogeneity from 2001 to 2023. The combined proportion of cities with cold islands and strong heat islands remained stable at approximately 60%, and the spatial scope of the SUHI effect generally exhibited an expansion trend characterized by “widespread dispersion and localized clustering.” (3) Natural environmental and human activity factors jointly shaped the driving pathways of the SUHI effect. The cumulative contribution of key influencing factors such as built-up height, the kernel normalized difference vegetation index, annual average temperature, and nighttime light intensity reached 76.4%, exhibiting significant temporal heterogeneity and spatial nonlinearity. (4) The effect of HUE on the SUHI effect followed a cascade process of “direct driving—interaction enhancement—threshold constraint—pathway transmission.” No statistically stable HUE intensity threshold was identified at the national scale, whereas in the second quadrant, two independent methods consistently indicated that the marginal warming effect of HUE tends to saturate once its intensity exceeds 0.27. This study proposes differentiated policy recommendations, providing an important reference for mitigating the thermal effects of HUE and promoting sustainable urban development.

title: Automated camera parameters estimation and occlusion-aware visibility mapping of urban CCTV using asynchronously acquired MMS LiDAR
summary: Pre-installed urban CCTV cameras form a dense, city-wide sensing network with significant potential for urban geospatial monitoring. However, most deployed units lack accurate camera parameters including position, orientation, and Field of View (FoV) geometry, which prevents their systematic integration into urban geospatial information systems. This study presents a fully automated pipeline that estimates these parameters and produces occlusion-aware visibility polygons as Geographic Information System (GIS) vector outputs from asynchronously acquired Mobile Mapping System (MMS) Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) point clouds. The pipeline needs no on-site access, no physical calibration targets, and no prior knowledge of the camera’s interior orientation, viewing direction, or lens distortion. The only positional input is an approximate horizontal camera location, such as that recorded in a municipal camera inventory or measured with consumer-grade GNSS. A coarse-to-fine strategy bridges the radiometric and temporal gaps between the LiDAR data and the optical imagery. Installation heights are inferred from the geometric signature of the pole in the point cloud, the approximate viewing direction is found by intensity-image matching on rendered panoramas, and precise 2D-3D correspondences are then established by deep feature matching with multi-stage spatial filtering. Camera parameters (interior orientation, exterior orientation, and radial distortion) are jointly estimated with a photogrammetric projection model that requires no initial approximations. An occlusion-aware visibility module then casts 3D rays against the full point cloud to separate ground that the camera can actually see from ground hidden by buildings and vegetation, and the boundaries are exported as GIS-ready vector polygons. Experiments on 21 urban CCTV cameras give a mean 3D camera position error of 0.85 m (σ = 0.33 m) despite a six-month gap between the MMS survey and the CCTV imagery. The resulting visibility polygons reach a mean Intersection over Union (IoU) of 0.721 against manually delineated ground truth. On the common 20-camera subset used for the manual baseline, the proposed method reduces the mean 3D position error by 81.2% (0.87 m versus 4.62 m) and is more accurate for 19 of the 20 cameras, supporting its reliability for large-scale deployment.

title: PGD-Net: Prompt-Guided Hybrid Transformer Decoder for building extraction from remote sensing images
summary: Accurate building extraction from remote sensing imagery is essential for urban planning, cadastral mapping, and geographic information updating. However, existing methods still struggle with semantic degradation during feature decoding, small-building detection, and accurate boundary delineation. To address these issues, we propose PGD-Net, which integrates feature-conditioned prompt guidance into the decoding process for building extraction. The proposed method introduces learnable internal feature prompts to compensate for degraded building semantics. These prompts are further integrated into a hybrid Transformer decoding framework to guide feature reconstruction. Furthermore, a two-level optimization strategy is adopted: TOAM enhances small-building feature responses at the feature level, while a lightweight morphological post-processing step is applied at the output level to refine predicted masks and alleviate boundary discontinuities. Experiments were conducted on three public benchmark datasets, including Massachusetts, WHU, and Inria, as well as the newly constructed Xiamen Building Dataset (XM). PGD-Net achieved IoU scores of 76.81%, 92.05%, and 84.18% on the Massachusetts, WHU, and Inria datasets, respectively. It also delivered the best performance on the XM dataset, which contains a large number of dense urban village buildings with severe occlusions and shadows. The results demonstrate that PGD-Net effectively improves extraction completeness, boundary accuracy, and small-building detection performance in complex urban environments. The code is available at https://github.com/dawnlight129/PGD-Net.

title: RSFF: a reconciliation-sparse fusion framework for semantic segmentation of rocky desertification land in multimodal time series
summary: Accurate identification of rocky desertification land (RDL) is crucial for ecological environment monitoring and management in karst regions. However, RDL extraction is often hindered by land-cover confusion, seasonal variability, and the fragmented, small, and irregular spatial distribution, when existing methods insufficiently exploit multi-temporal multimodal information. To address this issue, we construct the first dual-modal RDL semantic segmentation dataset with time series (RD dataset) and propose a reconciliation-sparse fusion framework (RSFF) for multi-temporal multimodal data. The framework adopts a dual-branch encoding architecture with multilevel spatio-temporal interaction to separately extract spatial and temporal features from optical and Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imageries. Through the designed Convolutional Attention Reconciliation Module (CARM), multidimensional enhanced features are reconciled, and the Sparse Cross Fusion Module (SCFM) is employed to improve feature discriminability while reducing computational complexity compared with conventional dense attention mechanisms, enabling deep complementarity of cross-modal information. Experimental results on the RD dataset demonstrate that RSFF can effectively distinguish RDL from similar land-cover types, such as bare land and cropland, and significantly enhance RDL boundary delineation while maintaining high classification consistency. The mean intersection over union (mIoU) and overall accuracy (OA) reach 82.94% and 94.28%, respectively, outperforming other state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods. In addition, experiments on the public PASTIS-R dataset further verify the robustness of RSFF under different landscape characteristics and small, fragmented parcel distributions. The RD dataset and code are available at https://github.com/laopiao-lp/RSFF.

title: Seasonal asymmetric changes between photosynthesis and canopy structure phenology across the northern hemisphere
summary: Vegetation phenology is a critical indicator of terrestrial ecosystem responses to climate change. However, our understanding of the asynchrony between photosynthetic and canopy structural phenology remains limited. Using satellite-derived datasets of gross primary productivity (GPP) and leaf area index (LAI) from 1982 to 2018, we systematically quantify this phenological asynchrony across the Northern Hemisphere (>30°N). At the primary 50% relative-amplitude threshold, GPP-derived transition dates preceded the corresponding LAI-derived transition dates by 7.02 d in spring and 17.51 d in autumn on average, although spring offsets were more spatially variable. During the study period, ΔSOS had a trend of −0.584 d decade−1, indicating a widening spring lead of the GPP-derived transition. By contrast, ΔEOS had a trend of + 0.643 d decade−1, indicating a narrowing autumn offset. Boosted regression tree models identified spring temperature as the climate variable most strongly associated with spring asynchrony, whereas autumn asynchrony showed comparable associations with autumn temperature and solar radiation. Our findings provide phenological evidence for a seasonally asymmetric and shifting structure-function relationship in northern terrestrial ecosystems under climate change. Accounting for the asynchrony between photosynthetic and canopy structural phenology is thus essential for advancing satellite-based vegetation monitoring and carbon cycle modelling.

title: Beyond accuracy: environment-dependent performance and threshold robustness of spectral water indices across regions and seasons
summary: Spectral water indices are widely used for operational surface-water mapping, yet large-scale automation is often hindered by threshold uncertainty and limited cross-scene transferability. Existing studies typically rank indices by peak accuracy while overlooking the critical trade-off between maximal performance and sensitivity to threshold perturbations. Here we establish a broad multi-region, multi-season benchmark using Sentinel-2 imagery, covering 12 environmentally heterogeneous regions and four seasons (48 scenes). Twelve representative indices are assessed in terms of scene-adaptive peak accuracy (F1max) and threshold robustness, quantified by a newly proposed Robustness Smoothness Index (RSI). We also introduce PCA-Bridge, which embeds scenes using environmental variables only and maps performance and robustness landscapes in the resulting environmental space. Rather than identifying a single universal index, our analysis reveals a clear trade-off between peak accuracy and threshold robustness. While a median F1max>0.92 across 48 scenes suggests generally high performance, performance declines markedly in complex environments, particularly those dominated by snow and ice. NDWI attains high peak accuracy (F1max≥0.95) in 50.0% of scenes but shows low robustness (RSI≥0.75 RSI≥0.75 RSI≥0.75 in only 8.3%), indicating strong threshold sensitivity. By comparison, MBWI and AWEInsh achieve the highest median F1max (0.968 and 0.960), whereas WI2015 and NWI exhibit the strongest robustness overall, with the nhighest mean RSI (0.840 and 0.837) and broad robustness coverage (RSI≥0.75 RSI≥0.75 RSI≥0.75 in 87.5% of scenes). These findings support task-oriented index selection rather than one-size-fits-all ranking. Out-of-scene transfer experiments showed that scene-wise optimal performance does not guarantee threshold generalisation. Overall, the proposed framework helps identify when peak accuracy, robustness, and transfer performance align or diverge, supporting more reliable large-scale surface-water monitoring.

title: A review of remote sensing for agricultural drought: technologies, indices, modelling advances and future prospects
summary: Agricultural drought is a complex hazard that jeopardises food security and progress toward the Sustainable Development Goals. We systematically reviewed peer-reviewed English-language literature published between 2015 and 2025, focusing on Remote Sensing (RS)-driven agricultural drought monitoring and prediction. Eligible studies were identified from the Web of Science and Scopus databases (last searched in August 2025); review articles, duplicates, and irrelevant studies were excluded, resulting in 181 articles. This review critically examined the evolution of sensors, drought indices, modelling approaches, and emerging technologies used to assess agricultural drought across diverse agro-ecological regions. Specifically, we (1) systematically evaluated the use of optical, thermal, and microwave RS platforms, along with satellite-based, model-based, and reanalysis products for agricultural drought monitoring; (2) reviewed widely used RS-based drought indices, including single indices grouped into nine categories, as well as composite indices; (3) reviewed software or programming languages applied; (4) assessed the progression of modelling approaches from traditional statistical and time-series methods to machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) frameworks; and (5) examined validation strategies applied to agricultural drought assessment. The analysis reveals a growing research interest in this topic, with a strong geographic concentration in Asia, particularly China. Optical and thermal platforms (e.g. MODIS and Landsat) dominate the literature (~54%) due to their accessibility, followed by satellite-derived precipitation products (17%), while microwave soil-moisture missions remain underutilized (~7%). Regarding RS-based indices, most studies employed more than one index: 44% analysed multiple individual indices, 51% used composite indices (either alone or in combination with individual indices), and only 5% relied on a single index. Vegetation indices, such as NDVI, remain workhorses; however, their sensitivity to soil background effects and canopy saturation has driven increased adoption of thermal composites (e.g. VHI), as well as adaptive weighting schemes and principal component analysis-based approaches. Moreover, computational tools used in drought research can be broadly grouped into geospatial and RS platforms for large-scale data processing and analysis (e.g. QGIS, GEE), and general-purpose programming languages (e.g. R, Python) for model development and advanced analytics. Regarding the methodology, statistical and time-series approaches account for 64% of the reviewed studies, followed by ML models (20%) and DL methods (15%), while explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) remains nascent. Techniques, such as random forests, support vector machines, and CNN and LSTM architectures, generally outperform traditional models but require large training datasets and raise concerns related to interpretability and ethics. In terms of validation, hydro-climatic indices such as SPI and SPEI are most commonly used (32%), followed by crop yield and yield anomaly data (19%). This review further identifies key research gaps across sensors, indices, and modelling approaches and proposes a roadmap for developing equitable, interpretable, and resilient agricultural drought monitoring systems. Emerging opportunities include context-aware and interpretable AI, multi-sensor and multi-scale data fusion across optical, thermal, and microwave domains, integration of physiologically meaningful indicators such as sun-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF), robust uncertainty quantification, and the development of hybrid and physics-informed modelling frameworks.

title: SAMWater: a prompt-guided multimodal framework for transferable water mapping with the segment anything model
summary: Accurate and transferable surface water mapping is critical for water resource assessment, flood monitoring, and aquatic ecosystem management, but remains difficult because SAR speckle, optical contamination, heterogeneous backgrounds, and scarce high-quality pixel-level annotations limit robust large-scale mapping. We propose SAMWater, a prompt-guided multimodal framework that integrates Sentinel-1 SAR, Sentinel-2 optical imagery, the Segment Anything Model (SAM), and Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM 3). Instead of using SAR and optical data as independent classifiers, SAMWater transforms their complementary information into structured prompts for coarse-to-refined water segmentation. A physically interpretable multisensor coarse water prior is first generated from Sentinel observations using an automatic threshold-based strategy. This prior is then refined through prompt-based boundary refinement, a multi-prompt excavation strategy that derives point, box, and Gaussian-style mask prompts, and Water-IoU fine-tuning for water-specific candidate ranking. Using globally distributed samples and manually interpreted PlanetScope reference labels, SAMWater achieved average Kappa coefficients of 90.71%, 85.63%, and 89.05% in evaluations stratified by water body type, land cover background, and climatic zone, respectively. It generally outperformed traditional thresholding and clustering methods, public deep learning models, and existing global water or land cover products, particularly in structurally complex river, reservoir, urban, agricultural, and mountainous scenes. Ablation experiments confirmed that multimodal prior fusion, structured prompt construction, and water-specific ranking jointly drive the performance gains. Moreover, SAMWater-generated refined labels improved the training of U-Net, DeepLabV3+, and SegFormer, indicating their utility for weakly supervised segmentation. SAMWater therefore demonstrates that integrating physically interpretable remote sensing priors with promptable foundation models provides a practical pathway for transferable surface water mapping, large-scale multisensor weak-label generation, and more consistent monitoring of surface water extent.
